class: SPARSE_BINARY: keep the top `density` of weights per group by |w|, zero the rest, binarise survivors with a per-group scale. Stored as index+sign per survivor plus one fp16 scale per group: density*(log2(group)+1) + 16/group bits per weight. The ONLY family measured in this campaign that can go below one bit per weight.
HEADLINE_the_target_is_BYTE_REACHABLE: sparse0.05-g128 measures 0.8744 complete EBPW -- BELOW the 1.0 target, and the first time any representation in this campaign has crossed it. Its perplexity is 41.34 against a gate of 3.617, its median 4-gram repetition is 0.9892 against 0.0538, and it emits 96 identical tokens in a row. The bytes are reachable. Nothing that survives is.
SPARSITY_IS_DOMINATED_BY_QUANTISATION: At ~4 EBPW: sparse0.5 ppl 6.373 vs affine q4-g64 ppl 3.044 (which PASSES). At ~2.3-2.4: sparse0.25 ppl 11.477 vs affine q2-g128 ppl 4.085. Magnitude pruning at 50% density already costs more capability than 3-bit quantisation of everything. Sparsity extends the BYTE frontier below binary but is dominated on capability everywhere the two overlap.
the_cosine_collapse_is_monotone_here: 0.8984 -> 0.8224 -> 0.6540 -> 0.5086 as density falls. Unlike the calibration and residual results, cosine tracks capability cleanly WITHIN this class -- which is consistent with it being a coarse cross-class screen that fails as a fine within-class ordering.
WHAT_THIS_SETTLES_FOR_G010: Eight representation classes have now been measured on O003: affine, outlier-split, binary, pooled-calibrated binary, per-expert-calibrated binary, residual binary, sparse binary, and the bf16 source. The <=1.0 target is byte-reachable (0.8744 measured) and capability-unreachable by every one of them. The capability-preserving floor stands at 3.2831 EBPW, 3.8x the target.
CAVEATS: Magnitude pruning, one-shot, no retraining or error feedback. Sparse methods that recover accuracy normally require fine-tuning, which is Odyssey II work and was not done.
No sparse kernel exists, so no TPS; the arms reconstruct to dense bf16.
Index cost assumes log2(group) bits per survivor with no entropy coding of the index stream.
